data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The smallest positive integer satisfying x\u22613 (mod 5) and x\u22614 (mod 7) is 18.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the Bezout coefficients are mistakenly taken as the final x value (yielding 3 or -2) rather than as multipliers for k and j, 18 would be missed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If an algebraic manipulation error in 5k - 7j = 1 incorrectly yields k=5 and j=3, substituting back would wrongly produce 28.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Solve the linear Diophantine equation 5k + 3 = 7j + 4. Rearranging yields 5k - 7j = 1. Since gcd(5, 7) = 1 divides 1, a solution exists. The extended Euclidean algorithm gives the Bezout identity 3*5 + (-2)*7 = 1, yielding a base solution (k=3, j=2). Substituting k=3 back into 5k + 3 gives 5(3) + 3 = 18. The complete solution family is x \u2261 18 (mod 35), making 18 the smallest positive integer.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
